title: Al-Infitar: the sky cleaves
hookLine: what deceived you about your generous Lord, who made you and shaped you (82:6–8)

cards: A hand resting on a table, palm up. Small bones. Tendons that slide like cables.
A thumb that can touch every other fingertip, which is how a hand holds a pen, a cup, a baby's head. A hand is so familiar it mostly gets noticed when something goes wrong: a sprain, a cut, a cast.
The surah just before Al-Mutaffifin opens with the sky tearing apart, and then, in the middle of that chaos, asks a strangely personal question, about you and the body you're sitting in.

teach.h: FOUR WHENS: SKY, STARS, SEAS, GRAVES.
teach.b: Surah eighty-two begins with four whens. When the sky is cleft apart, infatarat, split like a seam. When the stars are scattered.
When the seas are made to burst. When the graves are overturned. Then every soul will know what it sent ahead and what it left behind.
Then verse six, in Pickthall's words: "O man! What hath made thee careless concerning thy Lord, the Bountiful, Who created thee, then fashioned, then proportioned thee?"
The Lord here is al-Karim, the Generous, the Noble. The question isn't angry. It's almost puzzled.
What fooled you? What made you forget the One generous enough to make you? Then three verbs, a craftsman's sequence.
Created you. Fashioned you, made you complete.

Proportioned you: 'adalak, from the same root as 'adl, justice, balance. Two eyes, two ears, two hands, a body in balance, like a scale set level. Verse eight: in whatever form He willed, He put you together.
Look back at the week. Al-Buruj, faith under fire, and al-Wadud, the Loving. Al-Inshiqaq, the sky split and the human toiling toward his Lord, and the record in the right hand.
Al-Mutaffifin, full measure and the rust on hearts.

Now the sky cleaves again, and between the splitting sky and the recording angels the surah mentions later, it stops to point at something close at hand: a human body, created, fashioned and proportioned, sitting right here.

how: Al-Infitar is one of the short surahs of the Qur'an's last part; its question, what made you careless of your generous Lord, is quoted as a gentle call to gratitude, and its verses on the noble recording angels shape how Muslims think about their deeds.

o: the fig, a fruit of the holy land
the dawn, a new day breaking over the land
the cleaving, the sky split open like a seam

games.q: what's inside the verses — tap the pairs.
p: the sky split like a seam

s: the question in 82:6 is spoken in anger
it's almost puzzled: what fooled you about your generous Lord?
'proportioned you' shares a root with the word for justice
'adala and 'adl: balance, like a scale set level.
Al-Infitar mentions noble angels who record deeds
later in the surah (82:10–12): noble, writing, knowing what you do.

games.q: the sky is cleaving, the stars scatter. then the surah asks you one question. what is it?
o: what made you careless of your generous Lord?
how many good deeds did you do?
games.why: What hath made thee careless concerning thy Lord, the Bountiful (82:6): followed by created you, fashioned you, proportioned you.

practice: Hold one hand in the other and feel the bones of the fingers, the soft pad of the palm, the pulse at the wrist; move each finger slowly, and notice how much is working without being asked.
Let a word of thanks come, in whatever language you think in. If you pray, you can say alhamdulillah.

wordCard.voice: Al-Infitar. The cleaving, the sky split open, and the name of Surah eighty-two, which asks what made you careless of your generous Lord. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the Generous, the Noble, a name of God; Pickthall renders it the Bountiful in 82:6.

carryVoice: Your line: shaped in proportion. Your hands were made, and balanced. Two hundred ten, and counting.
